notes: Large clear photograph of the Van Osdel–designed Tucker/Byron L. Smith house on the NW corner of 22nd: dark brick with stone bands, three tall conical-roofed round/polygonal corner towers with cresting and finials, Gothic gabled dormers, clustered chimneys; tall iron picket fence on brick piers with ball finials; an iron-and-glass arched porte-cochère/entrance canopy on the 22nd Street (south) side. At right (north) a rough-faced stone house with a conical-roofed rounded bay — very probably 2130 Murdoch (H. I. Cobb, 1890) — and beyond it a long three-storey brick row. Overhead trolley wires and rails in 22nd Street, a cast-iron street lamp at right, a man with a bicycle. Strong 1904 evidence: shows the corner, the fence, the canopy and the trolley wires; date window inferred c. 1890–1911. Compared with the pre-1881 Greene stereograph, the towers here carry tall conical slate roofs — a later remodelling, after 1890 (the cresting-crowned towers still stood next to the 1890 Murdoch house in a20-glessner-vanosdel-2140-photo); whether 1904 had spires or cresting is unresolved — date this photo before choosing. The 1898 Van Osdel book plate (a20-aic-quarter-century-tucker-residence) still shows the cresting state, which (if the photo was current in 1898) would put the spires after 1898.
